proposed.explanation: Size is not the defining characteristic. A small plaza can be a node; a tall building can be a landmark. Conversely, a large district is neither node nor landmark. This is the fundamental distinction. Nodes are strategic focal points where you GO TO, GATHER, or PASS THROUGH (decision points, hubs, junctions). Landmarks are external reference points you LOOK AT for orientation without entering. The key: nodes are entered/participated in; landmarks are observed/referenced. Historic vs. modern is irrelevant to Lynch's classification. Any object can be a landmark if it serves as a visual reference. Location (center vs. periphery) is not the defining characteristic.
